verdicts.summary: server_running treats a zombie as running only when ps can report state. Where ps cannot show the state, a crashed managed server whose parent never reaps it is never replaced, and disconnect cannot clear it either. Before this commit the same state recovered.
verdicts.missing: The checkout does not contain ps, so the exact ps behaviour on BusyBox is unverified here; the first reviewer assumes BusyBox ps rejects -p. Whether the remote's PID 1 reaps orphans is environment-dependent and not readable from the repo.
evidence: packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:623-630 (server_running; zombie only detected via ps output)
packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:671-673 (runtime PID equal to recorded managed PID skips the adopt probe)
packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:711-723 (live-looking server, 60s wait, exit 1, files kept)
packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:739-743 (managed PID/port/managed files written by the launcher)
packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:780-789 (stop script exits 1 while kill -0 still succeeds on a zombie)
apps/server/src/serverOwnership.ts:89-90 (lock is released by the OS on SIGKILL)
apps/server/src/serverOwnership.ts:118-127 (runtime file cleared only in the release finalizer, which a SIGKILL skips)

verdicts.summary: The lock makes the unconditional delete safe: ensureEnvironment holds withTargetLock (tunnel.ts:1725-1728), and the stale entry is read under that same lock (tunnel.ts:1647). The finalizer's identity check at tunnel.ts:1587 skips the remote stop, so no remote stop runs. The only gap is interruption between the delete and the close, which is finding 1.
verdicts.missing: Real SSH connect and auth time, remote login-shell startup (sh -l), and per-invocation node startup on the remote. The outer 90s timer counts all of these (command.ts:306).
evidence: packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:1771-1785 (disconnect holds the same lock; uninterruptible pair)
